extracted.intended_audience: picture-book authors and illustrators; aspiring creators of children's picturebooks
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for creating children's picturebooks emphasizing the collaborative author–illustrator process, visual storytelling, trim/typographic design, pacing, and how visuals and text interact to shape narrative and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create opportunities for the illustrations to do the storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: A big part of writing a picture book manuscript is to create opportunities for the illustrations to do the storytelling; 'picture book writing is the art of finishing an unfinished thing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leave space in the text for the illustrator to solve visual problems (e.g., what spectacular things the characters miss, how falling should look). Be economical in text so pictures can carry action, mood, and detail. Anti-pattern: over-describing everything in text and leaving no work for the pictures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let trim size affect layouts and type placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The book's trim size should affect the layouts, and the type placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design page composition and typography with the physical dimensions in mind (e.g., composition working its way up the page as characters dig down). Sketch layouts early (even on a napkin) and consider how type lines can track characters. Anti-pattern: treating text layout as independent of page proportions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing and page turns — pick the moments between events
rubrics_metrics.description: For books you have to pick the moments between the events so you can picture the action that connects them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose still moments that imply motion rather than attempting to show continuous action (what animation might show). Example: instead of depicting a continuous fall, show the moment before/after to let readers imagine the motion. Anti-pattern: trying to depict too much sequential action across spreads so the book reads like an animation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use whitespace to signal limits and build tension
rubrics_metrics.description: White space below them showed up and moved closer and closer over a few spreads — using whitespace to indicate approaching the end of the dig.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ white space intentionally to show boundaries, absence, or escalation (e.g., the 'bottom' approaching). It can create suspense and visual rhythm. Example: a growing blank area beneath characters to imply depth or limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain deliberate misalignment between text and pictures (textual obliviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sam and Dave would be unaware of these changes, and the text would not acknowledge them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let pictures carry ironic or additional information that the text ignores to produce deadpan humor or layered meaning. This can reward attentive readers and create comic or poignant effects. Anti-pattern: having the text over-explain what the pictures already show, which flattens the interplay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a character aware of pictorially-presented information (the 'aware' agent)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there's any information in the pictures that the characters in the story are ignorant of, it helps a lot to have someone in the book be aware of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce a character (e.g., the dog) who notices what the reader sees but protagonists do not; this warms the experience, prevents excessive creepiness, and can steer tone toward comedy rather than bleakness. Use that character to validate or react to visual differences. Anti-pattern: leaving pictorial revelations unacknowledged by anyone in the story, which can feel unsettling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid events that happen while characters sleep (risk of dreamlike ambiguity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anything that happened while they were asleep ended up looking like it was a dream — we needed somebody who was awake throughout to fix that problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want events to be perceived as 'real' by readers, avoid staging them during sleep/unconsciousness unless you intend a dreamlike ambiguity. Instead ensure a witness or keep characters awake to anchor causality and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise text to accommodate strong visual ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: There were a few times I changed the text because you had a visual idea that was funny or compelling ... a visual idea necessitated a revision to the text that ultimately gave Sam and Dave's relationship more depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open to reworking the manuscript after seeing illustrations or roughs; visual solutions can suggest better emotional beats, pacing, or characterization. Collaboration may produce textual changes that strengthen the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use simple repeating motifs and escalate them
rubrics_metrics.description: The first thing they missed was always a diamond ... as soon as I thought of just growing the diamonds every time they missed one, the big spread with the giant diamond came up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor a clear, repeatable visual gag or motif that escalates across the book (growing diamonds example) rather than switching disparate items that dilute focus. Escalation creates payoff and a satisfying visual climax. Anti-pattern: introducing many unrelated objects that divide attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compose typography to follow visual movement
rubrics_metrics.description: The composition working its way up the page the deeper they got, and the text on the facing page following them until both sides got to the top.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider creative type placement as part of visual storytelling — text lines can echo character movement or align with page composition to reinforce pacing and joke timing. The final design needn't be perfectly uniform, but well-placed moments can be especially effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design endings as subtle variations of the start
rubrics_metrics.description: They would tumble down through that space and land somewhere that looked a lot like the place they started, but was different in subtle ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan conclusions that mirror the opening but introduce small, visual alterations to create a twist or emotional resonance while maintaining structural cohesion. Let the pictures show the differences while the text may remain oblivious for comedic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let visual constraints drive story decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: We were talking about books where the stories are kind of inextricably linked to their trim size or dimensions, and we started talking about a book that would go up or down as the main visual idea for the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow physical and visual mechanics (trim size, page orientation, pacing opportunities) to inform the story premise and its jokes. Designing around a visual conceit can produce a stronger, more integrated picturebook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative hybrid process — iterate together rather than hand off finished text
rubrics_metrics.description: It was a weird hybrid of what you do collaboratively and how you work when you're both writing and illustrating the book yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work iteratively with illustrator early and often (sharing roughs, layout sketches) instead of delivering a finished text expecting no change. This hybrid approach enables text to shift in response to visual discoveries and yields a more cohesive book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reward attentive readers with visual payoffs and subtle discoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: Attentive readers will be rewarded with a rare treasure in this witty story of looking for the extraordinary – and finding it in a manner they'd never expect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hide visual rewards, small changes, or Easter eggs that attentive readers can spot (e.g., growing motifs, subtle differences at the end). These rewards create reread value and reader satisfaction. Anti-pattern: making everything explicit on first read so there's no incentive to return to the book.
